## Research Experience

**Search for Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in Gamma-Ray Bursts** *(Sep. 2026 – Present)*  
*Supervisor: Prof. Ersin Göğüş (Sabancı University) — Remote*

* Analyzing Fermi/GBM light curves across different time intervals and energy bands using Python and `Stingray`.
* Modeling power spectra with power-law continua and Lorentzian profiles to characterize candidate QPO features.
* Applying Gaussian Process modeling to characterize stochastic variability and test candidate QPO signals.
* Investigating the energy dependence of candidate signals and comparing results with published studies.

**Quasi-Periodic Oscillation Analysis of V1405 Cas Using TESS Photometry** *(Oct. 2025 – Present)*  
*Supervisor: Prof. Ersin Göğüş (Sabancı University) — Remote*

* Studying quasi-periodic oscillations in V1405 Cas, a dwarf nova cataclysmic variable, using TESS photometry.
* Identified two additional post-outburst TESS sectors, extending the temporal baseline for tracking variability across pre-outburst and post-outburst phases.
* Fitting Gaussian and Lorentzian models to frequency–power spectra and estimating detection significance and upper limits.

**Connectivity Conditions for Nagaoka Ferromagnetism in Honeycomb Lattices** *(Dec. 2025 – May 2026)*  
*Supervisors: Prof. Alev Devrim Güçlü (İzmir Institute of Technology) & Asst. Prof. Emir Haliki (Ege University)*

* Conducted a theoretical and computational study of the connectivity condition in Nagaoka ferromagnetism for finite honeycomb lattices.
* Constructed triangular and hexagonal honeycomb clusters with zigzag and armchair edge terminations.
* Modeled the one-hole Hubbard limit as a connected state graph and applied breadth-first search (BFS) algorithms to evaluate state reachability under nearest-neighbor hopping.

**Exoplanet Light Curve Formation and Calibration with TESS Photometry** *(Jan. 2024 – Present)*  
*Supervisor: Asst. Prof. Tansu Daylan (Washington University in St. Louis) — Remote (@AstroMusers)*

* Processing TESS-SPOC and QLP light curves in Python for data cleaning, detrending, normalization, and transit extraction.
* Running Box Least Squares (BLS) periodogram analyses to recover orbital periods, transit durations, and transit depths.
* Validating recovered parameters against ExoFOP-TESS and literature values, identifying discrepancies caused by noise, detrending choices, and period aliases.
* Calculating expected timing precision from finite light-curve baselines for an upcoming publication.

## Internships

**Undergraduate Research Intern** *(Aug. 2025 – Sep. 2025)*  
*İzmir Institute of Technology (IZTECH)*

* **Topic:** Graphene Quantum Dots – Tight-Binding
* Built and solved tight-binding models starting from a six-site ring up to finite hexagonal and triangular flakes with zigzag and armchair edges.
